uses: Relieves mild to moderate pain such as headache, toothache, body ache, and muscle pain
seriousWarnings: Doses higher than recommended can damage the liver
Avoid combining with other paracetamol-containing products
commonInteractions: Warfarin: occasional use is usually safe; regular high-dose use may increase bleeding risk
patientFriendlyExplanation: Paracetamol is one of the most commonly used medicines to bring down fever and ease mild pain. It is safe at the dose your doctor recommends.
evidenceSource: WHO Essential Medicines List; product information leaflets

uses: Relieves symptoms of allergic rhinitis (sneezing, runny nose, itchy eyes)
seriousWarnings: Avoid driving or operating machinery if drowsiness occurs
Use with caution in patients with kidney impairment — dose may need adjustment
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to cetirizine or hydroxyzine
Severe renal impairment without dose adjustment
commonInteractions: Alcohol or other sedatives may increase drowsiness
patientFriendlyExplanation: Cetirizine helps relieve allergy symptoms like a runny nose, sneezing, watery eyes, and itching. The most common side effect is mild drowsiness.
evidenceSource: Product information leaflets; standard pharmacology references

uses: Replaces fluid and electrolytes lost due to diarrhoea, vomiting, or excessive sweating
commonSideEffects: Mild nausea when taken too fast
seriousWarnings: Use cautiously in patients with kidney disease or severe heart failure
Do not use as a substitute for IV fluids in severe dehydration
contraindications: Persistent vomiting that prevents oral intake
commonInteractions: No major drug interactions when used as directed
patientFriendlyExplanation: ORS replaces the water and salts your body loses during diarrhoea or vomiting and is the first-line treatment to prevent dehydration.

uses: Treats bacterial infections of the ear, nose, throat, urinary tract, skin, and chest
seriousWarnings: Stop and seek medical help if you develop hives, swelling of the face, or difficulty breathing — these can indicate a serious allergic reaction
Complete the full prescribed course even if you feel better
commonInteractions: May reduce the effectiveness of oral contraceptive pills
patientFriendlyExplanation: Amoxicillin is a common antibiotic used to treat bacterial infections. It does not work against viruses such as the common cold or flu.
evidenceSource: WHO Essential Medicines List; product leaflets

uses: Treats certain bacterial infections of the chest, throat, sinuses, skin, and some sexually transmitted infections
seriousWarnings: May affect heart rhythm in patients with existing heart-rhythm disorders — inform your doctor of any cardiac history
contraindications: History of cholestatic jaundice with azithromycin
commonInteractions: May interact with certain heart medicines and antacids — check with your doctor or pharmacist
patientFriendlyExplanation: Azithromycin is an antibiotic that treats certain bacterial infections. It is usually taken once a day for a short course.

uses: Treats acid reflux (GERD), gastritis, and stomach/duodenal ulcers
seriousWarnings: Long-term use may be associated with low magnesium and vitamin B12 levels — discuss with your doctor if used beyond 3 months
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to pantoprazole or other PPIs
commonInteractions: May reduce the absorption of medicines that need stomach acid, such as certain antifungals
patientFriendlyExplanation: Pantoprazole reduces the amount of acid your stomach makes, easing heartburn, reflux, and ulcer symptoms.

uses: Reduces inflammation in conditions such as arthritis, muscle injury, and menstrual pain
seriousWarnings: Can cause stomach ulcers or bleeding, especially with prolonged use
May affect kidney function in patients who are dehydrated or have existing kidney disease
Use with caution in patients with high blood pressure or heart disease
commonInteractions: May increase the effect of blood-thinning medicines
May reduce the effect of some blood-pressure medicines
patientFriendlyExplanation: Ibuprofen is a common pain and fever medicine that also reduces inflammation. Take it with food to reduce stomach upset.
evidenceSource: WHO Essential Medicines List; NSAID prescribing guidelines
